slot.brief: Two gases effuse through the same pinhole; use time or distance data to find the molar mass ratio of an unknown gas — moderate ratio computation.

stem: Equal volumes of nitrogen and an unknown gas effuse through the same pinhole under identical conditions. If their effusion times are $20\ \text{s}$ and $30\ \text{s}$, respectively, find $M_{\text{unknown}}/M_{\text{N}_2}$.

verdicts.working: For equal volumes, effusion time is proportional to √M. Thus M_unknown/M_N₂ = (30/20)² = 9/4.

working:
For equal volumes, $\dfrac{t_X}{t_{\text{N}_2}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{M_X}{M_{\text{N}_2}}}$; $\dfrac{M_X}{M_{\text{N}_2}}=\left(\dfrac{30}{20}\right)^2=\dfrac{9}{4}$.

Independent check: For equal volumes, effusion time is proportional to √M. Thus M_unknown/M_N₂ = (30/20)² = 9/4.
solution:
For equal volumes, effusion time is proportional to the square root of molar mass.
$$\frac{t_{\text{unknown}}}{t_{\text{N}_2}}=\sqrt{\frac{M_{\text{unknown}}}{M_{\text{N}_2}}},\qquad \frac{M_{\text{unknown}}}{M_{\text{N}_2}}=\left(\frac{30}{20}\right)^2=\frac{9}{4}.$$
